bear.reason: Bear mechanisms from review/counter.json, each sized from company evidence: (1) credit: Stage 2 rose 10.1% -> 11.9% of gross, NPL 90+ 6.9% (seven-quarter high) and Brazil household defaults at a record 8.1%; cost of risk normalizes up as loan growth slows and IFRS 9 front-loading stops masking losses, taking ROE from the tax-normalized 26-27% to 21% at the start and to 15% by year 5, below Nu's own FY2023 18% level; (2) tax: the 2026 deferred-tax benefit does not recur and CSLL rises to 20% from 2028 (about 1-2 points of ROE); (3) BRL: about 91% of revenue is Brazilian and the real fell about 10% intraday after the 2026-10-25 election, so USD book growth carries translation losses beside retained profit: start 13% (vs 19% base), within retention 21% x (1 - 26%) = 15.5%, fading; (4) capital: CET1 11.9% and falling forces slower RWA growth. Payout floor stays the evidenced 26% buyback share (H1 2026).

base.terminal_reason: Terminal ROE 16% stays above the 11.2% cost of equity because Nu's own lowest post-breakeven ROE was about 18% (FY2023: net income 1,030.5m on average parent equity about 5.65bn) and its cost-to-serve / efficiency advantage is reported every quarter (efficiency ratio in the Q2 2026 release); the 16% sits two points below that own low to allow for the CSLL rise and competition, not a peer number.
base.reason: ROE: tax-normalized own run rate. H1 2026 net income 1,932.5m was booked at an 11.8% tax rate (Q2 14.2% with a one-off deferred-tax benefit) against 25.8% in FY2025 (income tax 996.7m on pretax 3,868.4m); at the FY2025 rate H1 profit is about 1.63bn, about 3.25bn a year, about 26.5% on average H1 parent equity (11.29bn -> 13.25bn); FY2024 28.1% and FY2025 30.3% on average equity (reported). Start 27%, year 5 25% after CSLL rises to 20% from 2028 (about 1-2 points). Book growth: own common equity grew about 26%/yr 2021-25, 33%/yr 2023-25 and 13.8% in H1 2026 alone ex-AOCI (about 29% annualized); the start is held at 19% (below that history) because the Brazilian conglomerate's CET1 fell 13.0% -> 11.9% in six months as RWA grew 14.7% vs CET1 capital +5.4% (excess over the minimum 1.85bn): growth is limited by the capital the business retains, fading to terminal growth. Payout floor 26% = H1 2026 buybacks 500.4m / net income 1,932.5m (US$1.0bn program to June 2027, 499.6m left; no dividend).

bull.terminal_reason: Terminal ROE 20% above the 11.2% cost of equity: in the bull Nu keeps its reported ROE (FY2025 30% on average equity, Q2 2026 33% reported) through scale in Brazil and the Mexico bank license (CNBV authorization 2026-07-09, 15.8m customers, loan-to-deposit 35% with room to lend), so the terminal is set at its own 2024-25 level less a third for tax and competition.
bull.reason: ROE: start 30% (reported FY2025 30.3% on average equity; H1 2026 about 31.5% reported, 26.5% tax-normalized, so the bull assumes the credit models keep cost of risk flat while ARPAC keeps rising +37% y/y), year 5 31% as Mexico (revenue +79% y/y in Q2 2026) matures. Book growth start 22% within retention 30% x (1 - 26%) = 22.2%, below the own 2023-25 26-33%/yr, capped by the CET1 room (11.9%, excess 1.85bn). Payout floor 26% = H1 2026 buyback share.

regulatory_capital.reason: Q2 2026 6-K capital note, Nu Prudential Conglomerate (Brazil): RWA 35,710,139k; minimum capital required 3,749,565k = 10.5% of RWA (the requirement with the conservation buffer, as the filing computes it); CET1 4,262,877k = 11.9% (13.0% at 2025-12-31), excess margin 1,848,040k. Nu Holdings itself has no regulatory capital requirement; CET1 sits in the regulated Brazilian (and Mexican, 14.9% vs 10.5%; Colombian, 15.3% vs 10.5%) entities, so the consolidated common book used here is only a PROXY: it is about three times the conglomerate's CET1, so the engine's check on it is loose and the real binding limit is the conglomerate's 11.9% CET1, which is why book growth starts below Nu's own history.

bear.reason_he: Nu היא בנק, ולכן התשואה היא על ההון העצמי. בתרחיש הדובי מחזור האשראי בברזיל (פיגורי משקי בית בשיא 8.1%, NPL 90+ ב-6.9% ועלייה בשלב 2) והעלאת CSLL ל-17.5% ואחר כך 20% מחזירים את התשואה על ההון לרמת 2023 (18%) ומטה. התשואה הגבוהה עוד לא הוכחה לאורך מחזור אשראי מלא, ולכן המכפיל יורד.

base.reason_he: Nu היא בנק, ולכן התשואה נמדדת על ההון העצמי (ROE). היא הייתה 28% ב-2024 ו-30% ב-2025. במחצית הראשונה של 2026 היא כ-29% אחרי נרמול המס הנמוך של הרבעון השני (14.2% מול 25.8% ב-2025). מס CSLL גבוה יותר וההון שהצמיחה דורשת (CET1 ירד מ-13.0% ל-11.9%) מורידים אותה לכ-26%. זה עדיין הרבה מעל מחיר ההון, ולכן מכפיל גבוה מוצדק שיורד ככל שהצמיחה מאטה.

bull.reason_he: בתרחיש השורי Nu שומרת על תשואה על ההון של כ-32% גם במס רגיל. זה דורש שהמרווח המותאם לסיכון יישאר קרוב לשיא של 12.4%, שעלות הפיקדונות תישאר נמוכה (88% מהריבית הבין-בנקאית) ושמקסיקו, שהפכה לבנק באוגוסט 2026, תעבור מאיזון לרווח. התשואה השולית על ההון ב-2023 עד 2025 הייתה כ-38%, אבל זה עוד לא הוכח לאורך מחזור.

bear.event_he: פיגורי משקי הבית בברזיל בשיא של 8.09% (ספטמבר 2026) ופיגורי 90+ של נו עולים מעל 7.5%: הפרשות להפסדי אשראי צומחות מהר מהתיק והתשואה על ההון יורדת לכיוון 20%.
יחס ההון הליבה (CET1) ירד מ-13.0% ל-11.9% בחצי שנה: אם הירידה נמשכת, נו תאלץ להאט את צמיחת האשראי או לעצור את הרכישה העצמית.
אחרי ניצחון לולה הריאל נחלש בכ-10% ביום אחד: כ-91% מההכנסות בברזיל, ולכן כל היחלשות מתמשכת של הריאל מקטינה את הרווח וההון בדולרים כמעט אחד לאחד.
המס על חברות האשראי (CSLL) עולה ל-20% מ-2028 והטבת המס של 2026 לא חוזרת: הרווח הנקי נמוך בכ-15% מהקצב של רבעון 2.
הבנק המרכזי מגביל שיווק אשראי לא מבוקש מ-2027: גיוס לקוחות והגדלת מסגרות אשראי מואטים.
תחלופה בהנהלה (סמנכ"ל כספים הוחלף, סמנכ"ל טכנולוגיה התפטר) פוגעת בביצוע בדיוק כשמחזור האשראי מתהפך.

base.event_he: תיק האשראי ממשיך לגדול בקצב גבוה (39.4 מיליארד דולר, +44% בשנה) עם מרווח ריבית מותאם סיכון באזור 10-12%, כפי שההנהלה אמרה ('באותו אזור').
שיעור המס חוזר לכ-26% (כמו 2025) ולכן הרווח השנתי נמוך מ-4 כפול רבעון 2; תשואה מנורמלת על ההון כ-26-28%.
יחס היעילות נשאר סביב 20% ב-2026, כפי שההנהלה הנחתה, למרות ההשקעה במקסיקו ובארה"ב.
הסליק יורד בהדרגה (13.75% בספטמבר 2026): עלות המימון יורדת, הכנסות הצף נשחקות, והביקוש לאשראי נתמך.
השלמת תוכנית הרכישה העצמית של מיליארד דולר (נותרו 499.6 מיליון עד יוני 2027) מקזזת את הדילול מתגמול במניות.

bull.event_he: מקסיקו, בנק מלא מאוגוסט 2026, מכפילה את חלקה בהכנסות (7.2% היום, +79% בשנה) עם פיקדונות מבוטחים ומשכורות.
הבנק המרכזי בברזיל מאשר את רכישת Banco Porto Real ונו מקבלת רישיון בנק מלא, בלי דרישת הון נוספת.
פיגורי 90+ יורדים מתחת ל-6.5% בזמן שהתיק ממשיך לגדול, והתשואה על ההון נשארת מעל 30% גם אחרי נרמול המס.
ההשקה בארה"ב ו-Nu Global הופכות לעסק עם הכנסות משמעותיות עד 2029.

key_risk.reading_he: מחזור האשראי הצרכני בברזיל: נו הגדילה בכוונה את החשיפה ללווים מסוכנים יותר, פיגורי 90+ הגיעו ל-6.9% (הגבוה בשבעה רבעונים), ההפסדים הצפויים עלו 46% בשנה, ופיגורי משקי הבית בברזיל בשיא של 8.09%. במקביל יחס ההון הליבה ירד ל-11.9%. רבעון חלש באשראי יפגע ברווח ובצמיחה יחד.

bottleneck.reading_he: NU is not a supply bottleneck: Pix and Open Finance are open public rails, so access is not scarce. What is scarce is cheap, well-underwritten funding and low cost to serve, where NU leads: deposits US$45.3B at 88% of the interbank rate (-3 pp y/y), cost to serve US$1.0 per active customer per month, efficiency 19.5%. Capacity is being added by rivals in the same unsecured consumer segment: Mercado Pago credit book +75% y/y (US$16B), Inter loans +29%.

future.reading_he: Large, concentrated, still-growing pool: NU puts the retail revenue pool of Brazil, Mexico and Colombia at US$227.9B with NU about 5% of it, and banking concentration (HHI 889 Brazil, 993 Mexico vs 328 US). Mexico is under-penetrated (about 37% of adults with formal credit, 16% with a bank card) and management's illustrative gross-profit-pool CAGR is about 15% for Mexico vs about 8% for Brazil (not guidance). Direction in Brazil is mixed near term: household default on market-rate credit hit a record 8.09% in September 2026 (6.89% a year earlier) and Selic is still 13.75%.

moat.note: Cost and funding moat, evidenced against Itau (ROE 24.3%, Brazil efficiency 35.5%) and Inter (ROE 16.3%, efficiency 42.1%): NU earns ROE 33% at 19.5% efficiency with deposits at 88% of interbank and US$1.0 monthly cost to serve. ROIC is not computable for a bank (forensic roic unavailable); ROE ran 27-33% for seven quarters. Not access-based: Pix/Open Finance are open, and Mercado Pago is closing in on credit growth.

switching_costs.note: Pix, Open Finance and salary portability make switching easy in both directions; NU keeps customers through engagement and price, not lock-in.

retention.note: Monthly activity 83.5% held while customers grew 13% y/y; ARPAC US$12.5 to 17.1 (+22% FXN), so cohorts deepen rather than churn. Inter: 58.3% active.

pricing_power.note: NIM rose to 22.9% and risk-adjusted NIM to 12.4%, but management ties it to mix toward unsecured and higher-risk segments, not to price increases; payroll loans are rate-capped and incumbents compete on price.

customer_concentration.note: No customer is 10% of revenue (139M retail customers). Geographic concentration is the real concentration: Brazil 91% of revenue (see geopolitics).

market_size.note: NU puts its serviceable retail revenue pool at US$227.9B with about 5% share; Mexico under-penetrated, NU's Mexico gross-profit share under 1% of a US$43B pool (company analysis).

competition.note: Intense: Mercado Pago book +75% in Brazil and Mexico, Inter +29%, Itau and BBVA Mexico profitable incumbents. NU still grows fastest in net income and customers among the Brazil names.

substitutes.note: Open rails let any digital bank replicate the account and Pix (NU about 20% of Pix transfers, Inter about 9%); the substitute risk is other digital lenders, not a new technology.

management.note: Delivery is good: first US$1bn+ quarter, efficiency guided to about 20% for FY2026 and 19.5% in 2Q26, Mexico bank launched. Depth is the concern: new CFO Rob Livingston (from July 2026; change sourced from press) and CTO resignation effective 2026-11-12 with the founder-CEO interim. No numeric guidance track record (gap).

capital_allocation.note: US$500.4M of buybacks in 1H26 (avg about US$12.31) vs SBC US$216.8M, so net shrink; no dividend. But Brazil prudential CET1 fell 13.0% to 11.9% in six months (RWA +14.7%), and the US launch is a new cost centre with no revenue yet; Monzo talks denied.

governance.note: Founder David Velez holds about 74.4% of voting power through Class B shares; foreign private issuer (no Form 4). Managerial P&L since Q4'25 is reconciled to IFRS, but the 2Q26 IFRS tax rate of 14.2% (27.6% a year earlier) is not explained in what was read.

regulation.note: Net headwind in Brazil: CSLL to 17.5% then 20% from 2028, credit-marketing limits from 2027, payroll-rate caps, Brazil bank licence (Banco Porto Real) pending BCB approval. Positive: Mexico full bank licence live since August 2026.

technology_ai.note: NuFormer model in production on three credit portfolios, AI agents handle over 60% of Brazil support conversations, cost to serve US$1.0/month. CTO departure is a key-person watch item.

geopolitics.note: About 91% of revenue in BRL, reported in USD; the 25 Oct 2026 election moved BRL about 10% intraday and Brazilian equities sharply; fiscal deficits flagged by analysts. Diversification (Mexico 7%) is small.

market_direction.reading: Large, concentrated, still-growing pool: NU puts the retail revenue pool of Brazil, Mexico and Colombia at US$227.9B with NU about 5% of it, and banking concentration (HHI 889 Brazil, 993 Mexico vs 328 US). Mexico is under-penetrated (about 37% of adults with formal credit, 16% with a bank card) and management's illustrative gross-profit-pool CAGR is about 15% for Mexico vs about 8% for Brazil (not guidance). Direction in Brazil is mixed near term: household default on market-rate credit hit a record 8.09% in September 2026 (6.89% a year earlier) and Selic is still 13.75%.

bottleneck_potential.reading: NU is not a supply bottleneck: Pix and Open Finance are open public rails, so access is not scarce. What is scarce is cheap, well-underwritten funding and low cost to serve, where NU leads: deposits US$45.3B at 88% of the interbank rate (-3 pp y/y), cost to serve US$1.0 per active customer per month, efficiency 19.5%. Capacity is being added by rivals in the same unsecured consumer segment: Mercado Pago credit book +75% y/y (US$16B), Inter loans +29%.

share_trajectory.reading: NU is still taking share: customers 122.7M to 138.9M (+13% y/y), about 118M in Brazil (62% of adults at FY2025, customer growth above the five largest incumbents combined per BCB data in the 20-F); 2Q26 net income +49% vs Itau +7.8% and Inter +34%; Mexico revenue +54% in FY2025 (523.1 to 808.1M) and +79% y/y in 2Q26 (175.7 to 314.6M). The one named rival growing credit faster is Mercado Pago (book +75%, Mexico fintech MAU +45%).

competitive_position.reading: Stronger than Itau and Inter on returns, cost and engagement: ROE 33% vs Itau 24.3% vs Inter 16.3%; efficiency 19.5% vs Itau Brazil 35.5% vs Inter 42.1% (definitions differ); monthly activity 83.5% vs Inter 58.3% active clients. Weaker on credit quality: NPL 90+ 6.9% vs Itau 1.9% and Banorte 1.5%, a riskier low-income unsecured book. Against Mercado Pago NU is larger and more profitable but MELI grows its credit book faster and has the e-commerce data and distribution.

threats.reading: Regulation and tax: CSLL for certain financial companies rises to 17.5% from April 2026 and 20% from 2028 (Brazil is about 91% of revenue); BCB resolutions of 23 Oct 2026 limit unsolicited credit marketing from 2027 (a customer-acquisition and limit-increase lever); INSS payroll loans are rate-capped. Country risk: the 25 Oct 2026 election moved BRL about 10% intraday. Competition: Mercado Pago (+75% book) and Inter in the same segment; Open Finance and salary portability lower switching. Credit: record household default in Brazil.

bottlenecks.reading: What NU supplies is competition and low cost to serve in concentrated, high-fee banking. Banking concentration (HHI 2024-25) is 889 in Brazil, 993 in Mexico, 1,262 in Colombia against 328 in the US, 373 in Germany, 488 in France (NU's own table from BCB, CNBV, SFC, ECB data). NU claims cost to serve and G&A per active customer about 85% below Brazilian incumbents (internal analysis; incumbents have 1,685 to 3,955 branches). This gap does not close quickly because incumbents' branch and legacy-system costs are structural; the counter is that Itau already earns ROE 24.3% at 35.5% efficiency, so incumbents are not fragile.

Mexico is an under-penetrated credit market: 63% of adults have a bank account, about 37% formal credit, 16% a bank credit card (INEGI ENIF 2024 / Dec 2025); top five issuers hold about 85% of card portfolio. NU reached 9.2M credit-card customers in 2025 (+35%), about half with no prior card, and over 5% of card purchase volume (Banxico). The scarce step was the bank license: CNBV gave Nu Mexico its operations authorization on 2026-07-09 (search excerpt of Nu's 6-K of 2026-07-10), which allows full deposit and credit products; Mexico was 6.8% of FY2025 revenue (US$808.1M), loan-to-deposit ratio only 35% in 2Q26. BBVA Mexico (loan growth about 10%) and Mercado Pago (Mexico fintech MAU +45%) add capacity at the same time.

Brazil's public rails lower the barrier for every entrant: Pix reached US$6.3 trillion in 2025 (+29%, 179.7M users), NU originates close to 20% of Pix transfers (BACEN), Inter reports about 9% Pix share (2Q26 filing excerpt). Open Finance and salary portability make switching easier for NU's customers as well as incumbents'. Open rails mean the moat is cost, data and primary-bank engagement, not access.

The scarce thing that limits growth is cheap, well-underwritten funding and credit quality, not demand: NU's 90+ day NPL was 6.9% in 2Q26 (up 35 to 40 bps in the quarter, book +37% FXN to US$39.4B) against Itau 1.9% and Banorte 1.5%, a different, much riskier book (low-income, unsecured). Mercado Pago grows its book +75% (credit cards +91%) and Inter +29%, so competitors are adding capacity in the same unsecured consumer segment.

Hypothesis: regulatory and fiscal policy in Brazil (taxes on financial institutions, interest or payroll-loan rate caps, Selic path) is the largest external swing for NU's margin; the 20-F payroll-loan note says INSS payroll loans are capped against Selic. A search headline of 2026-10-26 to 11-01 reports a 20% one-day NU share fall after a Brazilian election result; not read, cause and content unverified.
